title: Meta-Rational Pragmatics

sourceEvidence.locator: The distinction an agent cannot yet make
sourceEvidence.excerpt: An assistant encounters two histories: access was granted and then revoked, or revoked and then granted. The people, resource and event types are identical, but the correct decision changes when the last operation prevails. A representation containing only the event set cannot support that distinction. Understanding this task requires both information preserving order and a procedure that uses it correctly.

sourceEvidence.locator: The distinction an agent cannot yet make
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Meta-Rational Pragmatics proposes investigating understanding through such executable distinctions. Its central wager is that an agent can diagnose what its current representation cannot distinguish, construct a suitable interpreter, verify the improvement and retain the procedure for reuse. This is an engineering research program. A mathematical limit on lost information does not establish that the proposed architecture outperforms alternatives or explains human cognition.

sourceEvidence.locator: The distinction an agent cannot yet make
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Sufficiency therefore means sufficiency for a declared family of questions or tests. If two equally likely histories receive the same representation but require opposite answers, a predictor restricted to that representation cannot exceed 50% expected accuracy on the pair, even through randomization. A new program may compute the missing distinction from retained history. If that history has been discarded, more computation cannot reliably reconstruct it.

sourceEvidence.locator: The distinction an agent cannot yet make
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Representations can be understood as partitions: their classes identify differences the system ignores. Refinement separates previously confused cases while preserving earlier distinctions. Yet richer representation can increase cost, and a useful result still needs a valid interpretation contract. An operation returning the last known event cannot silently supply the last event in the world. Proof, testing and assumptions about input completeness remain separate obligations.

hook: Grant access, then revoke it; reverse those steps, and the right answer changes.
readerPromise: Recognize the distinction between possessing facts and being able to use them correctly.
protectedRevelations: Detailed proofs, architectural commitments and experimental prescriptions.
visualPlan: The order changes everything: Show the same access card receiving grant then revoke in two clear ordered steps. Set a second history beside it with the order reversed and the permission outcome still covered. Align the two event sets, making the missing order visibly important.

What an answer forgets: Reveal a small ordered record beside a simpler record that loses the sequence. Let the proposed agent mark the missing order and attach a possible procedure for checking it. Keep a test card visibly pending beside the proposed procedure.

Understanding that can improve: A reviewer compares the two histories and the decisions each would allow. Return to the closed and open entry possibilities beside the book, without a completed capability claim.
